action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design, groups parameter handling), pain points (existing feature selection limitations), and acceptance criteria (concrete use cases, API usability, extensibility). Questions grounded in sklearn_2021q4 context and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirements elicitation practices.

Generated 10 Socratic interview questions using 5W1H framework targeting SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter requirement. Questions decompose: user workflow goals, abstract class necessity, stakeholder pain points, pipeline integration context, behavioral expectations, acceptance criteria, alternative trade-offs, and edge case handling. Designed to elicit concrete requirements from Issue #21356 fragments and establish shared understanding before SRS formulation.

Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class pattern, groups parameter support), pain points (current workflow limitations), and acceptance criteria (success definition, trade-offs). Questions decompose the SequentialFeatureSelector requirement into concrete, answerable prompts grounded in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Business need: Standardized, production-ready feature selection with grouped data support. Pain points center on manual selection inefficiency and data leakage risks in grouped datasets. Solution requires abstract selector base class and groups parameter in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to enable systematic, auditable feature engineering workflows.

End-user confirms critical need for abstract feature selector base class with groups parameter support to enable consistent, leakage-free feature selection across time-series and hierarchical production datasets, addressing manual selection inefficiency and cross-validation compliance gaps.

End-users require a standardized abstract base class for feature selectors with groups parameter support in fit() to eliminate manual selection bottlenecks, enable time-series/hierarchical data handling, and support reproducible, auditable ML workflows in production environments with compliance requirements.

Clarifying seven critical ambiguities: (1) abstract class design scope and inheritance model, (2) groups parameter implementation pattern and data-leakage detection, (3) prioritization of three selection strategies, (4) integration depth for time-series/hierarchical support, (5) estimator pluggability constraints, (6) guidance output format (visual vs programmatic), and (7) API contract enforcement across selector implementations.

Five clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in the SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement: abstract class design pattern, groups parameter validation scope, MVP strategy prioritization, interpretability/guidance requirements, and estimator compatibility constraints.

EndUser clarification questions identify six critical ambiguities: (1) abstract class design scope and inheritance strategy, (2) groups parameter implementation semantics versus automation, (3) MVP scope for three selection strategies, (4) pluggable estimator contract and feature importance extraction, (5) automated versus manual data leakage prevention, and (6) backward compatibility with existing SequentialFeatureSelector. These clarifications are essential before requirements can be formalized into system specifications.

End-user confirms core pain points (manual selection inefficiency, grouped data support gap) and refines abstract class design to extend sklearn base classes with groups parameter support. MVP scope: forward/backward strategies with GroupKFold-compatible groups parameter; recursive strategy and automated leakage detection deferred to Phase 2.

End-user confirms manual feature selection inefficiency and grouped data validation gaps as core pain points. AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector extending sklearn base classes with forward selection MVP and deferred recursive/backward strategies. groups parameter in fit() must follow GroupKFold semantics for production ML workflows with time-series/hierarchical data. Pluggable estimator support required for consistent cross-strategy interface.

End-user confirms need for AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector extending sklearn base classes with unified interface for forward/backward/recursive strategies. Critical requirement: fit() must accept groups parameter following GroupKFold pattern to enable grouped cross-validation and prevent data leakage in production ML workflows with time-series and hierarchical data. All three selection strategies required for MVP to address manual feature selection inefficiency.

Consolidated 10 structured interview records from EndUser dialogue on sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement (Issue #21356). Primary pain points: manual feature selection inefficiency and missing groups parameter for grouped data validation. Core functional requirements: AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector base class (extending BaseEstimator/SelectorMixin) unifying forward/backward/recursive strategies, plus fit() groups parameter following GroupKFold semantics. Three unresolved scope decisions require deployer confirmation: MVP strategy prioritization, base class extension details, and groups parameter validation scope. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 compliance achieved through functional requirement formalization and constraint documentation.

Eight hierarchical user requirements synthesized from interview records: 3 MUST-priority items addressing AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector base class design, groups parameter support, and method signature consistency; 2 SHOULD-priority items for forward/backward selection strategies and systematic guidance; 2 COULD-priority items for recursive strategy and estimator pluggability. All requirements traced to consolidated pain points (manual inefficiency, missing groups support) and validated end-user confirmations. Unresolved scope decision (IR-006) on three-strategy MVP delivery requires stakeholder prioritization before Phase 1 commitment.

Targeted dialogue probes deployer's infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, dependency versions, computational overhead), security mandates (compliance requirements, audit logging, data leakage prevention), and scalability expectations (dataset sizes, feature dimensionality, strategy prioritization for MVP vs. Phase 2 delivery). Questions apply MoSCoW prioritization and life-cycle trade-off reasoning to resolve IR-006 scope decision and validate AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector design against production ML workflow requirements.

Eight targeted questions probe infrastructure deployment constraints (environments, compatibility, serialization), scalability expectations for grouped datasets and strategy combinations, security/governance requirements for data leakage prevention and audit logging, backward compatibility with existing implementations, strategy prioritization impact on deployment phasing, integration with sklearn pipelines, performance thresholds for grouped cross-validation, and validation gate placement—all grounded in confirmed pain points (manual selection inefficiency, missing groups parameter) and refined requirements (AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector extending BaseEstimator/SelectorMixin).

Formulated 7 targeted questions probing infrastructure constraints (deployment environment, scalability, integration), security mandates (data governance, compliance, leakage detection), and scalability expectations (performance SLAs, parallel execution, strategy prioritization). Questions ground Deployer responses in concrete operational requirements for AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector with groups parameter support, enabling data-driven MVP scoping decisions and deployment risk mitigation.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for CPU-based Python scientific stack; mandates input validation and audit logging for groups parameter to prevent data leakage; targets 10K features/1M rows scalability; prioritizes backward elimination strategy for MVP Phase 1 (Phase 2: forward, Phase 3: recursive) balancing computational cost against production ML workflow requirements; requires edge-case handling and sklearn pipeline compatibility via standard base classes.

Deployer confirms CPU-based Python ML stack deployment with strict security validation of groups parameter, O(n_features × n_splits × estimator_time) scalability for 10k features/1M rows, MVP scope limited to forward selection with groups support, and backward compatibility with sklearn ≥0.24 via new AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector class.

Deployer response addresses infrastructure (Python/sklearn ≥0.24 CPU stack), security (groups parameter validation, input sanitization), scalability (O(n_features × n_splits × estimator_train_time) complexity for 10K features/1M rows), and operational procedures (groups parameter validation before GroupKFold, sklearn semantics compliance). Cost-performance trade-off recommends MVP scope: forward selection only with backward/recursive deferred to Phase 2, reducing development cost while addressing primary pain point of manual feature selection inefficiency.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications on AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector design: (1) inheritance model coupling risk with sklearn APIs, (2) groups parameter validation responsibility boundary, (3) MVP strategy prioritization (forward vs. all three), (4) security input validation scope, (5) scalability trade-offs across selection strategies. Recommend explicit prioritization decision: forward selection as Phase 1 MVP, backward/recursive deferred; groups parameter validation as strict input checking with caller responsibility for leakage prevention; inheritance via both BaseEstimator and SelectorMixin for sklearn ecosystem compatibility.

Six clarifications required to resolve MVP scope (strategy prioritization), inheritance architecture (dual base class confirmation), groups parameter semantics (automatic vs. strict validation), performance acceptance criteria (wall-clock time budget), security immutability scope, and GroupKFold API compatibility alignment. All clarifications are operationally critical for deployment target (sklearn ≥0.24, CPU-based, 10K features/1M rows).

Deployer requires five critical clarifications on AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector implementation spanning inheritance scope (dual BaseEstimator+SelectorMixin), groups parameter validation strategy (automatic vs. manual leakage detection), MVP scope prioritization (all three strategies vs. phased delivery), cost-performance trade-offs (inline vs. deferred validation), and security boundaries (read-only access enforcement). Current workspace contains contradictions between enduser_confirmations (all strategies), deployer_responses (backward elimination focus), and deployer_questions (scope ambiguity). Clarifications are prerequisite for proceeding to detailed design phase per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirements traceability.

Deployer confirms AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector deployment requirements: dual inheritance (BaseEstimator + SelectorMixin), groups parameter with strict validation (type/dimension checking, None-injection prevention), forward selection as MVP primary with backward elimination as Phase 1.5 secondary (recursive deferred Phase 2), O(n_features × n_splits × estimator_train_time) complexity target for 10K features × 1M rows on CPU-based Python stack (scikit-learn ≥0.24). Automatic data leakage detection deferred to Phase 2; MVP prioritizes GroupKFold semantics compliance with input sanitization.

Deployer confirms dual inheritance requirement, finalizes security validation for groups parameter, locks scalability constraints for Phase 1 MVP (forward selection primary, backward secondary), and resolves cost-performance trade-offs favoring forward strategy on CPU-based infrastructure per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deployment checklist.

Deployer confirms AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector deployment readiness with dual inheritance (BaseEstimator+SelectorMixin), validated security constraints on groups parameter, O(n_features×n_splits×estimator_train_time) complexity ceiling supporting 10K features/1M rows, and phased MVP scope (Phase 1: forward selection, Phase 1.5: backward elimination, Phase 2: recursive elimination). All infrastructure, security, and scalability requirements validated against Python scientific stack deployment target.

Operating environment specification for sklearn AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector MVP: CPU-based Python scientific computing stack (numpy/scipy/scikit-learn ≥0.24) supporting datasets up to 10,000 features and 1M rows; O(n_features × n_splits × estimator_train_time) performance ceiling; mandatory groups parameter validation with type/dimension checking and None-injection prevention; dual BaseEstimator+SelectorMixin inheritance for pickle serialization and sklearn compatibility; forward selection Phase 1 primary with backward elimination Phase 1.5 secondary pending complexity validation.

Consolidated system requirements for sklearn_2021q4 SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement: Implement AbstractSequentialFeatureSelector base class (dual inheritance: BaseEstimator + SelectorMixin) with groups parameter support for grouped cross-validation, consistent method signatures across forward/backward/recursive strategies, O(n_features × n_splits × estimator_train_time) complexity bound, strict groups parameter validation (type/dimension/injection checks), Python 3.6+ compatibility on CPU platforms supporting 10K features/1M rows, and pickle serialization. Phase 1 prioritizes forward selection; Phase 1.5 defers backward elimination pending performance validation; Phase 2 defers recursive elimination. All requirements traced to IEEE 830 format with source attribution.
